newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Chairman of Cyprus Hellenic Group resigns.
newsitem.headline: Chairman of Cyprus Hellenic Group resigns.

text.p: The chairman of the Cyprus-based Hellenic Group of Companies resigned on Wednesday in a dispute with the island's archbishop over management of the group, Greek Cypriot papers reported on Thursday.

In a brief statement Paschalis Paschalides cited disagreements with Greek Cypriot Archbishop Chrysostomos over management of the church-controlled companies. The group has controlling stakes in quoted companies Hellenic Bank, Vassiliko Cement and Keo.
Paschalides refused to elaborate on the reasons for his resignation.

Philelephtheros newspaper on Thursday suggested the decision was rooted in the archbishop's decision to sell 25 percent of Vassiliko cement to the Cyprus Cement Company belonging to businessman Stavros Galatariotis.
Last December Cyprus Cement failed in a bid to acquire shares in Vassiliko. At the same time Italcementi of Italy increased its stake in Vassiliko to 33 percent from 20 percent.
A Greek millionaire built up the Hellenic Group and its administration was passed to the Greek Orthodox Church of Cyprus after the island's independence.
A debate on the status of church control over the group is currently pending in parliament.
